ai.description: *Draco norvillii* reaches 20 cm in total length. It features a grey-brown body with dark mottling and orange-yellow patagia. Distinctive traits include a long, pointed dewlap and prominent skin folds.
ai.identificationRemarks: Distinguish *Draco norvillii* by the unique, elongated, and pointed shape of its lateral skin flaps (patagia), which are significantly more tapered than those of other Indian *Draco* species.
ai.habitat: *Draco norvillii* inhabits tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in Northeast India, typically found in the canopy of tall trees at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: *Draco norvillii* is primarily diurnal, spending its active hours gliding between trees to forage for ants and small insects while remaining camouflaged against bark.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Draco norvillii* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 2–5 eggs in a soil nest. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months, typically from April to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: Draco norvillii is endemic to the Brahmaputra Valley in Assam and parts of Arunachal Pradesh, typically inhabiting low-elevation tropical forests and tea plantations.
